<reason>CON won the live clash on the motion’s only novel word, “bypass.” PRO had a strong moral frame (responsibility without a holding rule) but never specified a mechanism that made third-party apps obey without the locked, attesting architecture CON named. CON’s status-quo-versus-novelty comparison, browser fork, and one-way risk weigh were cleaner ballot stories; PRO’s Rebuttal 2 clip and unresolved server/honor fork left that path standing.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON R1: existing parental tools already cover PRO’s benign case; the motion adds only bypass-proofing, which PRO then either restates as a suggestion or concedes as locked-down enforcement.</best_rebuttal>
